mainTopic: Resting (הנחה) for a fallen scroll, using a ledge in front of a window, and acting across domains on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer about a scroll that rolled off a roof. On a straight wall, the scroll is treated as resting on the ground once it is within three טפחים, and רבי יהודה disagrees because he requires real הנחה. The גמרא objects that this would make רבא's rule, that the רבנן also require real הנחה within three טפחים, fit only one side of a dispute. So it rereads the whole משנה as רבי יהודה with missing words: one turns the scroll over only on a sloping wall, where it truly rests, and on a straight wall one may always roll it back. A new משנה permits using a ledge in front of a window on שבת. אביי explains that the ledge sticks out over a רשות הרבים and the משנה means breakable objects, and a ברייתא supports him. The same ברייתא allows using an upper ledge only opposite the window. אביי explains that the windowsill fills that ledge out to four טפחים there. Another משנה allows moving objects in another domain without carrying them more than four אמות, but forbids urinating or spitting from one domain into another. The amud ends with רב objecting to a version of that משנה which forbids the first case, because it follows רבי מאיר instead of the רבנן.

steps.title: The straight-wall case: above or below three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: This finishes an earlier answer. On a wall that does not slope, a scroll end more than three טפחים off the ground may be rolled back. Below three טפחים, it must be turned face-down.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a wall that does not slope: if the end is above three handbreadths, he rolls it back to himself; if below three handbreadths, he turns it over onto its writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that started on the previous amud. It explains how the rule works when the wall is straight and not sloping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a straight wall, the hanging end of the scroll does not touch anything, so it is in the air. Above three טפחים it is not treated as resting, so he may pull it back. Below three טפחים, the rule of לבוד treats it as if it is lying on the ground. Then rolling it back would be like carrying it in, so he may only turn it face-down to protect its dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: A sloping wall that the scroll can lie on
He rolls it back up to himself
He turns it over so the writing faces down
Three handbreadths, the distance of לָבוּד (treated as touching)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of an answer. The first half, about the sloping wall, came on the previous amud. Do not read this line as a brand-new statement.

phrases.english: With a wall that is not sloping,
above three handbreadths, he rolls it back to himself;
phrases.notes: It is hanging in the air and is not considered resting anywhere.

phrases.english: below three handbreadths, he turns it over onto the writing.
phrases.notes: Within three, it counts as lying on the ground (לבוד).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer earlier, which split the cases by the type of wall.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (inclined vs. non-inclined wall)
steps.terutzMaskana: For a straight wall, three טפחים is the line; below it the scroll is treated as on the ground.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה disagrees: real resting is required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה. It explains that he requires an object to actually rest on something before it counts as resting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even if it is not lifted off the ground [more than a thread's width, he rolls it back]. Because we require resting on top of something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up רבי יהודה's view from the משנה and gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first answer, the תנא קמא holds that within three טפחים counts as resting on the ground. רבי יהודה disagrees: as long as the scroll is not actually touching the ground, it has not rested. So he may roll it back even when it is a thread's width away. This sets up a dispute between תנאים about whether לבוד is enough for הנחה.

keyTerms.meaning: Resting or placing, needed for the act of carrying on שַׁבָּת

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵינוֹ מְסוּלָּק מִן הָאָרֶץ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: even if it is not lifted from the ground, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: "except by a thread's width, he rolls it back."

phrases.english: Because we require resting on top of something.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ אֵינוֹ מְסוּלָּק מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי יהודה rejects the three-טפחים rule given in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה requires actual הנחה on something; being within three טפחים (לבוד) is not enough.

steps.title: Challenge from רבא: the רבנן also require real resting
steps.stepSummary: רבא said that even according to the רבנן, an object within three טפחים needs real הנחה. Under the current explanation, that would make רבא's rule follow only one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what רבא said, that within three handbreadths, according to the רבנן, resting is required — shall we say he stated his ruling according to only one side of a dispute between תנאים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from Steps 1–2, using a ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1–2 made the תנא קמא hold that within three טפחים counts as resting, without real הנחה. רבא, however, said the רבנן do require real הנחה even within three. If the תנא קמא disagrees, רבא would only fit רבי יהודה's side. The גמרא finds it unlikely that רבא said his rule according to just one side of a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא whose ruling is used as the challenge
Within three handbreadths of the ground
According to one side of a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: But then, that which Rava said:
within three, according to the Rabbis, resting is required,
phrases.notes: The רבנן disagree with רבי עקיבא, who holds that an object caught in the air counts as resting (קלוטה כמי שהונחה).

phrases.english: shall we say he stated his ruling according to [only one side of] the Tannaim?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in Steps 1–2 that the תנא קמא treats within three טפחים as resting.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא קמא considers a scroll within three טפחים to be resting without real הנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא assumes everyone, including the רבנן, requires real הנחה within three. The current reading turns this into a dispute between תנאים, which is unlikely.

steps.title: New reading: the whole משנה is רבי יהודה, with missing words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its first approach. It says the entire משנה follows רבי יהודה, and some words are missing. The ten-טפחים rule applies to a sloping wall. On a straight wall, one may roll the scroll back even under three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: it is all רבי יהודה, and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches: When was this said? With a sloping wall. But with a wall that is not sloping, even less than three handbreadths, he rolls it back to himself. For רבי יהודה says: even if it is lifted from the ground only a thread's width, he rolls it back to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that avoids the challenge from רבא. It rereads the משנה as one single opinion with missing words filled in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a sloping wall, the scroll actually lies on the wall within ten טפחים, so it is truly resting. That is why he must turn it over. On a straight wall it rests on nothing, so even under three טפחים he may roll it back. Since nobody in the משנה now treats within three as resting without real הנחה, רבא's rule fits everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire משנה follows רבי יהודה
And this is what it teaches
In what case was this said?

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: the ten-טפחים rule (turn it over) applies only to a sloping wall, where the scroll really rests. On a straight wall it is never resting, so one may always roll it back. This matches רבא's rule that real הנחה is required.
steps.confusionAlert: "רבי יהודה אומר" here is not a disagreement anymore. In the new reading it is the reason ("for רבי יהודה says") for the straight-wall ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps רבא's rule that real הנחה is required within three טפחים as something everyone agrees on, instead of one side of a dispute.

phrases.english: Rather: it is all Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
In what case was this said? With a sloping wall,
phrases.notes: The rule of turning it over once it is within ten טפחים.

phrases.english: but with a wall that is not sloping,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים גּוֹלְלוֹ אֶצְלוֹ.
phrases.english: even less than three handbreadths, he rolls it back to himself.
For Rabbi Yehuda says:
even if it is not lifted from the ground
except by a thread's width, he rolls it back to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation in Steps 1–2 because of the challenge from רבא in Step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה as one opinion with missing words (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה contains a dispute: the תנא קמא treats within three טפחים as resting, and רבי יהודה requires real הנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יהודה. Turning it over applies only to a sloping wall. On a straight wall one rolls it back even under three טפחים, so real הנחה is always required.

steps.title: Why the scroll may be rolled back on a straight wall, even under three טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason for the rewritten משנה's straight-wall ruling. On a straight wall the scroll is not resting on anything, and רבי יהודה requires real resting on a surface. So even below three טפחים, one may roll it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because we require the object to rest on top of something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why, on a straight wall, the scroll may be rolled back even when it is less than three טפחים from the ground. It answers that an object counts as resting only when it actually rests on a surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a straight wall, the scroll end hangs in the air and does not touch anything. Under רבי יהודה's view (Step 2), being close to the ground (within three טפחים) is not enough. The object must truly lie on something before it counts as הנחה, so it may be rolled back. On a sloping wall, by contrast, the scroll actually lies on the wall, which is why it must be turned over there. This fits רבא's rule from Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Placing / coming to rest (an object counted as having landed)
On top of something (a real surface)

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יהודה, being close to the ground does not count as resting. An object counts as resting only when it actually lies on a surface. That is why on a straight wall the scroll may be rolled back even under three טפחים, while on a sloping wall, where it lies on the wall, it must be turned over.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Asks for the logic behind the rewritten משנה's straight-wall rule (rolling back even under three טפחים).

phrases.english: Because we require resting on top of something.
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה's requirement of real הנחה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּבָעֵינַן הַנָּחָה עַל גַּבֵּי מַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the straight-wall ruling in the rewritten משנה from Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why may the scroll be rolled back on a straight wall, even when it is within three טפחים of the ground?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because רבי יהודה requires real resting on a surface, and a scroll hanging beside a straight wall is not resting on anything, even close to the ground.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The whole משנה follows רבי יהודה's requirement of actual הנחה.

steps.title: New משנה: using a ledge in front of a window
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on שבת one may place objects on a ledge in front of a window and take them off it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ledge that is in front of a window: one may place things on it and take things from it on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It allows using a ledge outside a window on שבת, both putting things on it and taking them off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ledge counts as its own area, ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, as the commentators explain. Moving objects between the house and the ledge is therefore permitted. The משנה does not say where the ledge sticks out to, and that is what the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: A ledge or projection sticking out from a wall
One may place and one may take

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A ledge that is in front of a window —
one may place on it and take from it on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may put objects on, and remove them from, a ledge in front of a window.

steps.title: Where does the ledge stick out to? Both options seem wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ledge sticks out to. Over a רשות הרבים, the משנה should forbid it, because the object might fall and be brought back in. Over a רשות היחיד, the rule is too obvious to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ledge, where does it stick out to? If you say it sticks out over a public domain, we should worry that the object might fall and he will come to bring it in. Rather, it sticks out over a private domain. But then the rule is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by laying out two possible cases. It shows that each one seems to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option 1 is a ledge over a רשות הרבים. The object could fall into the public street, and the person might forget it is שבת and carry it back into the house. That would be a real violation. Option 2 is a ledge over a רשות היחיד. There is no risk at all, so the משנה would be teaching something everyone already knows.
steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not about placing the object on the ledge. Placing it there is fine. The worry is that the object might fall into the street, and the person would then carry it back in from the רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on this משנה.

phrases.english: This ledge, to where does it protrude?
If you say it protrudes into a public domain —
we should be concerned lest it fall and he come to bring it in.
Rather, it protrudes into a private domain; that is obvious!
phrases.notes: Second option, which seems too obvious to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from Step 6 by asking which case it means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to put objects on the ledge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided challenge. A ledge over a רשות הרבים should be forbidden because of the risk of bringing a fallen object back in. A ledge over a רשות היחיד makes the rule too obvious to be worth teaching.

steps.title: אביי: the ledge is over the public domain, and the objects are breakable
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ledge does stick out over a רשות הרבים. The משנה is talking only about fragile objects, which would shatter if they fell, so there is no worry that someone will bring them back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, the ledge sticks out over a public domain. And what does the משנה mean when it teaches 'one may place on it'? It means breakable objects.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He keeps the first option, a ledge over a רשות הרבים, and limits the משנה to breakable objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a fallen object would be carried back inside. A fragile object that falls breaks, so there is nothing worth bringing back, and the worry disappears. This also means the משנה is not obvious, because it teaches a real permission over a רשות הרבים, limited to this kind of object.
steps.whatToRemember: The ledge sticks out over a רשות הרבים. The משנה allows placing only breakable objects on it, because if they fall they shatter and no one will carry them back in.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא: removing a worry by narrowing the case. Here the משנה is limited to the kind of object where the feared mistake cannot happen.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Actually, it protrudes into a public domain,
phrases.notes: Keeps the first option from Step 7.

phrases.english: and what is the meaning of 'one may place on it' that it teaches?
Breakable utensils.
phrases.notes: If they fall, they break, so there is no worry of bringing them back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם דְּמַפֵּיק לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of Step 7 by choosing the first option and narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers only to breakable objects.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ledge over a רשות הרבים should be forbidden in case a fallen object is brought back in.
steps.terutzMaskana: Breakable objects shatter when they fall, so the worry does not apply, and the משנה is not teaching something obvious.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up אביי: only fragile dishes are listed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists only breakable items (bowls, cups, small jugs, flasks) as allowed on a ledge over a רשות הרבים. This supports אביי's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: on a ledge in front of a window that sticks out over a רשות הרבים, one may put bowls and cups, small jugs and flasks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that אביי's answer is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the משנה allows only fragile objects on a ledge over a רשות הרבים. The ברייתא lists only glass and clay dishes, which break if they fall. This fits אביי exactly: nobody will bring a shattered dish back inside, so there is no worry of carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא that supports what was just said)
A ledge or shelf sticking out from a wall
Small jugs and flasks (all breakable dishes)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):
A ledge that is in front of the window
which sticks out into the public domain —
one may place on it bowls and cups,
phrases.notes: All breakable items, which supports אביי.

phrases.english: small jugs and flasks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in Step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the משנה refers only to fragile objects.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists only breakable dishes as allowed on a ledge over a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: using the whole wall, and the rule of two ledges
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds two rules. One may use the ledge along the whole wall, but not within the bottom ten טפחים. If there is a second ledge lower down, the lower one may be used everywhere, while the upper one may be used only opposite the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may use the ledge along the whole wall, down to the lowest ten טפחים. If there is another ledge below it, one may use the lower one. The upper one may be used only opposite his window.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא keeps going and gives new rules about where on the wall a ledge may be used. These rules set up the question the גמרא asks next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ledge may be used even far from the window, as long as it is not within ten טפחים of the ground. If there are two ledges, the lower one may be used along the whole wall. The upper one may be used only right in front of the window, and the גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: The bottom ten טפחים of the wall, closest to the ground
The lower one (here, the lower ledge)
The upper one (here, the upper ledge)
Directly in front of his window

phrases.english: And one may use (the ledge) along the entire wall
down to the lower ten handbreadths.
phrases.notes: Not within ten טפחים of the ground.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ זִיז אֶחָד לְמַטָּה מִמֶּנּוּ —
phrases.english: And if there is another ledge below it —
one may use it (the lower ledge),
but the upper one, one may not use
except opposite his window.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בְּכׇל הַכּוֹתֶל עַד עֲשָׂרָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and adds new rules that the גמרא will examine next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ledge may be used along the whole wall above the lowest ten טפחים. With two ledges, the lower one may be used everywhere, and the upper one only opposite the window.

steps.title: How wide is the upper ledge? Either way the rule seems wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of upper ledge the ברייתא means. If it is less than four טפחים wide, it should not be used at all, even in front of the window. If it is four wide, it should be usable along the whole wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this ledge? If it is not four טפחים wide, it is a מקום פטור, and he should not use it even opposite his window. If it is four wide, let him use it along the whole wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule that the upper ledge may be used only in front of the window. Neither possible width seems to fit that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ledge less than four טפחים wide is a מקום פטור, but it is too narrow, and things put on it will likely fall into the רשות הרבים. So it should be forbidden everywhere. A ledge four wide is a proper surface, so it should be allowed everywhere. Nothing seems to explain a rule of only opposite the window.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (asking for the exact situation)
Four טפחים, the minimum width for a real surface
An exempt area, too small to count as any רשות

steps.confusionAlert: Even though a מקום פטור is not a forbidden area in itself, the problem here is different. The ledge is so narrow that things will fall off it into the רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: This (upper) ledge, what is its case?
If it is not four handbreadths wide —
it is an exempt area,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כְּנֶגֶד חַלּוֹנוֹ נָמֵי לָא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: and he should not use it even opposite his window.
phrases.notes: Because objects would likely fall off.

phrases.english: And if it is four handbreadths wide —
let him use it along the entire wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from Step 10 that the upper ledge may be used only opposite the window.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule allowing the upper ledge only opposite the window.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible widths fail. Under four should be forbidden everywhere, and four or more should be allowed everywhere. Neither leads to a rule of only opposite the window.

steps.title: אביי: the windowsill fills out the upper ledge to four
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the lower ledge is four טפחים wide, while the upper ledge is less than four. The windowsill completes it to four. So in front of the window it counts as part of the window and may be used, but its sides may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the lower ledge is four טפחים wide, and the upper one is not four, but the window completes it to four. Opposite the window one may use it, because it is the back part of the window. To this side and that side it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by describing an in-between case. Here the upper ledge is narrow, but the windowsill adds to its width.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In front of the window, the narrow ledge joins with the sill to make a surface four טפחים wide. That part counts as part of the window. To the sides there is no sill, so the ledge stays under four and may not be used. This is exactly why the ברייתא allows the upper ledge only opposite the window.

keyTerms.meaning: The back part or extension of the window

steps.whatToRemember: A ledge narrower than four טפחים can still be used where the windowsill fills it out to four, because there it counts as part of the window. Elsewhere it stays forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: two surfaces can join together to reach the four-טפחים minimum, and then the combined area takes on the status of the window.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The lower one is four handbreadths wide,
and the upper one is not four handbreadths wide,
but the window(sill) completes it to four.
Opposite the window — one may use it,
because it is the back part of the window.
On this side and on that side — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תַּחְתּוֹן דְּאִית בֵּיהּ אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by describing a third, in-between case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the upper ledge is less than four wide, but the windowsill completes it to four.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The upper ledge must be either fully under four or fully four wide, so the ברייתא's rule seemed impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: The upper ledge is under four, but the windowsill completes it to four in front of the window. Only that part counts as part of the window and may be used.

steps.title: Moving objects in another domain while standing outside it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person standing in a רשות היחיד may move objects in a רשות הרבים, and the reverse. The limit is that he may not carry them beyond four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may stand in a private domain and move things that are in a public domain. He may also stand in a public domain and move things that are in a private domain. The condition is that he does not carry them beyond four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says you may reach over and handle objects that sit in a different domain from the one you are standing in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objects stay in their own domain, so nothing actually passes from one domain to the other. Moving them around inside their own domain is allowed. The one limit is not to carry them more than four אמות, since carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים is forbidden on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the most one may carry in a public domain on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The person does NOT bring the object into his own domain. He only moves it around where it already is. That is why this is allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A person may stand in a private domain
and move objects in a public domain.
Or he may stand in a public domain and move objects in a private domain,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יוֹצִיא חוּץ מֵאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: provided that he does not carry them beyond four cubits.
phrases.notes: Carrying four אמות in a רשות הרבים is forbidden on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹמֵד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּמְטַלְטֵל בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of ledges and windows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may stand in one domain and move objects located in the other domain, as long as he does not carry them beyond four אמות.

steps.title: No urinating or spitting from one domain into another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids urinating or spitting from a רשות היחיד into a רשות הרבים, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not stand in a private domain and urinate into a public domain. He may not stand in a public domain and urinate into a private domain. Likewise, he may not spit that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a contrasting case where crossing between domains is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous case the objects stayed in their own domain. Here, something actually leaves the person's body in one domain and lands in the other domain. That counts as transferring from one domain to another.

phrases.english: A person may not stand in a private domain
and urinate into a public domain,
nor stand in a public domain and urinate into a private domain,
and likewise he may not spit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וְיַשְׁתִּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 13. There the object stayed in its own domain, but here something actually crosses over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinating or spitting from one domain into the other is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יהודה on spit gathered in the mouth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that once spit has gathered in a person's mouth, he may not walk four אמות until he spits it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even once his spit has gathered in his mouth, he may not walk four cubits until he spits it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a stricter rule about spit. He treats gathered spit like an object being carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the spit has separated and gathered in the mouth, it is no longer just part of the body. Walking four אמות in a רשות הרבים with it would be like carrying any other object, so he must spit first.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached or gathered, said of spit that has collected

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three parts. Moving objects in another domain is allowed within four אמות. Urinating or spitting across domains is forbidden. רבי יהודה adds that gathered spit may not be carried four אמות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even once his spit has gathered in his mouth,
he may not walk four cubits
until he spits it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אַף מִשֶּׁנִּתְלַשׁ רוּקּוֹ בְּפִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the spitting rule of step 14 to walking with gathered spit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gathered spit counts like a carried object. One may not walk four אמות with it in a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: A reversed version of the משנה's opening line
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר שלמיא taught the משנה to חייא בר רב in front of רב with the opening line reversed: a person may NOT stand in a רשות היחיד and move objects in a רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חיננא בר שלמיא taught the משנה to חייא בר רב in front of רב this way: A person may not stand in a private domain and move objects in a public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a different wording of the משנה's first line, which makes it forbidden instead of allowed. This sets up רב's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says 'עומד אדם', meaning he may stand there and move the objects. This version says 'לא יעמוד', meaning he may not. Only the wording changed, but it flips the law.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. Our משנה says it is ALLOWED ('עומד אדם'). רב חיננא's version says it is FORBIDDEN ('לא יעמוד').

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelamiya would teach it
to Ḥiyya bar Rav in front of Rav:
A person may not stand in a private domain
and move objects in a public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first line of the משנה (step 13) and presents a reversed version of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב חיננא's version, standing in a רשות היחיד and moving objects in a רשות הרבים is forbidden.

steps.title: רב objects that this version follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב challenges רב חיננא: by teaching it as forbidden, he has left the majority view of the רבנן and followed the lone stringent view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Have you abandoned the רבנן and followed רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back against the reversed wording. He says it matches the minority view, not the accepted one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is stricter in this area. He worries that the person may end up bringing the object into his own domain. The רבנן do not share that worry, and the standard rule follows the majority. Teaching 'לא יעמוד' therefore sets the משנה against the accepted law.

keyTerms.meaning: And you acted or ruled like
The Sages, here the majority opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exact wording of a משנה matters, because one word can decide whether it follows the majority or a single dissenting view.

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
Have you abandoned the Rabbis
and followed Rabbi Meir?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the reversed wording reported in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חיננא בר שלמיא's version of the משנה ('לא יעמוד')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The forbidding version matches only רבי מאיר's lone stringent view. The halacha follows the majority רבנן, so the משנה should not be taught that way.
